title: Treasury Issues Proposed Rule to Implement Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act
body: October 22, 2026 WASHINGTON– The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) today issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to propose updates to the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) based on direction from Congress in the Comprehensive Outbound Investment Security (COINS) Act, passed as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.  The COINS Act codifies the U.S. Government’s approach to regulating certain outbound investments by U.S. persons and builds upon Treasury’s existing OISP. In passing the COINS Act, Congress made clear that restricting certain U.S. outbound investments into dual-use strategic technologies that benefit a foreign adversary’s military modernization efforts, surveillance states, and human rights abuses is necessary to prevent harm to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. President Trump is committed to protecting our national security and the implementation of the COINS Act is consistent with maintaining a strong, open investment environment that benefits our economy and supports our national security interests. The COINS Act directs the Secretary of the Treasury (the Secretary) to issue regulations that (1) require United States persons to provide notification to Treasury regarding certain transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in notifiable technologies, and (2) prohibit United States persons from engaging in certain other transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in prohibited technologies.  The COINS Act authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations with technical parameters for “prohibited technology” and “notifiable technology” in five technology sectors: semiconductor technologies and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems.  The COINS Act also authorizes the Secretary—in consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and subject to notice and comment rulemaking—to add and define technologies beyond those specifically listed in the law that enable the military, intelligence, surveillance, or cyber-enabled capabilities of a country of concern.  Accordingly, the Secretary has added biotechnology to the proposed regulations. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are committed to putting America’s national security first,” said Secretary Scott Bessent .  “The proposed regulations would strengthen the existing Outbound Investment Security Program to prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies that threaten U.S. national security.  This important step also helps promote our commitment to an open investment environment by providing clarity to U.S. and foreign investors as well as an opportunity for them to provide feedback on the proposed regulations.” “The proposed regulations are designed to address risks that can arise when foreign adversaries try to benefit from U.S. investment in key technology sectors,” said Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security Christopher Pilkerton.  Pilkerton added, “It will enhance the Outbound Investment Security Program and our efforts to protect U.S. national security.” The NPRM issued today provides details on key concepts and aspects of the program’s proposed implementation, including: Requirements applicable to a U.S. person (including any controlled foreign entities); Categories of covered national security transactions; Definitions; The scope of covered foreign persons; Excepted transactions; Technical specifications to inform the scope of covered national security transactions based on certain technologies and products in the areas of semiconductor technology and microelectronics, quantum information technologies, super intelligence systems, hypersonic systems, high-performance computing and supercomputing, and biotechnology; Information that a U.S. person is required to provide to Treasury as part of a notification; The process of requesting non-binding feedback and submitting confidential information; The knowledge standard and expectations for a U.S. person to conduct a reasonable and diligent inquiry prior to undertaking a transaction; and Conduct that would be treated as a violation of the proposed rule and applicable penalties for such conduct. Treasury invites comments from a wide range of stakeholders on all aspects of the NPRM including feedback on the scope of a covered national security transaction, definitions of key terms, the notification requirements, and the penalty and enforcement processes for violations, among other aspects.  Treasury will carefully consider this input before issuing the final implementing regulations. Written comments may be submitted by the deadline in the official NPRM, available at https://www.regulations.gov .  The NPRM will be followed at a later date by final implementing regulations, which will set an effective date for the program. The NPRM, fact sheet, and additional information are available at: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/international/outbound-investment-program .

title: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available
body: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available Today, we’re announcing the general availability of AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities . AWS Continuum is a security service that finds and validates code vulnerabilities, then delivers fixes as patches you can automate or as pull requests in your repositories. AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities confirms which findings are exploitable in your environment, ranks the resulting issues by business impact, and proposes a fix for each one. Every remediation starts in a mode where Continuum proposes the fix and a person approves it before it ships. In the future, you will be able to decide which actions Continuum can take on its own, within the guardrails you define. Using frontier artificial intelligence (AI) models, threat actors can turn a vulnerability disclosure into working exploit code in minutes, and the same tools that speed up development also increase the volume of findings your teams must process. If your organization runs a large application estate, your scanners likely produce thousands of findings a day, and many of them need no action. A finding can be unreachable, unexploitable, or already mitigated by a runtime control. Generic severity scores don’t tell you which resources a threat actor can actually reach, so a critical score on a dev-only utility looks the same as a medium score on a service one step away from a payments database. Previously, confirming whether a finding was exploitable took hours of manual investigation, and shipping a fix with confidence took days of coordination across security, infrastructure, and application teams, because the blast radius of a change is hard to assess without business context. To close that gap, Continuum proves which findings are exploitable and bounds the risk of each fix it proposes. Continuum builds a context graph from two primary sources: your code repositories and your AWS environment. For AWS, you set up a collector in the account and Region where your code runs. The collector gathers resource details such as AWS Config resources and network configuration so Continuum can judge whether a vulnerability is reachable over the network and what a threat actor could reach from it. From this graph, Continuum learns which systems are business-critical, who owns them, how services depend on one another, and which data each one touches. It uses that picture to identify your highest-value systems, such as customer data stores, payment pipelines, and authentication services, and then ranks each resulting issue by how close its attack path runs to those systems. Continuum analyzes each finding against your code and its environment context and assigns an evidence level, such as a verdict proven by static analysis of the vulnerable code path. For findings it can reproduce, Continuum runs the exploit in an isolated sandbox and attaches proof-of-concept code with the reproduction steps. It produces the attack path, the supporting source analysis, and a blast radius assessment instead of a risk score alone. It also evaluates whether your existing defenses would detect and stop the validated path. For each confirmed issue, Continuum generates a fix (a code patch, a dependency upgrade, or a configuration change) and opens it as a pull request in your connected repository, ready to review. Every fix requires human approval: you review and merge the pull request, so the final decision stays with your team. In the future, you will be able to build confidence in specific remediation classes and let Continuum apply those fixes automatically once its confidence gates pass, such as test coverage, scope bounds, and historical success rate. AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities in action To show how this works, I open AWS Continuum in the console and go to Code vulnerabilities . Before I can review issues, I set up an environment. I connect a code source, either a GitHub integration or an Amazon S3 bucket, and then create an environment that scans it on a schedule I choose. An Amazon S3 source has a couple of prerequisites: the bucket sits in the same account and AWS Region where I turn on AWS Continuum, and I grant access through an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that AWS Continuum assumes. I can optionally add AWS infrastructure context by setting up an AWS Continuum collector in the account and Region where my code runs and authorizing my environment to use it. For the full requirements and steps, see the AWS Continuum User Guide . The Overview page brings these pieces together in one place, showing my Code integrations , the Environments built on them, and the status of any AWS collector that supplies AWS resource context. I open one of my environments. The Issues tab lists validated, prioritized issues rather than raw scanner output, each with a severity, a status, and the time it was created. I choose one of the issues. The Overview rates it High severity, with the status Completed and the remediation already Delivered to GitHub. The Risk assessment explains why. Continuum rates its Exploitability as Exploitable , with an evidence level of Static proven and a validation run status of Completed . Likelihood is High , since the service is reachable from an attacker, requires no authentication, and needs no user interaction. Impact is Moderate , which means an attacker gains the ability to modify business data, with a blast radius reaching other users in the same tenant. A Proof section includes the source analysis behind the verdict. The Remediation section shows a fix already delivered as a pull request in GitHub, changing four files, with 50 lines added and 24 removed across the cart service. Continuum opens the fix as a pull request titled Continuum fix , and I choose View pull request to open it in GitHub. The console is explicit that a generated patch does not mean the issue is fixed. I still review and merge it, which keeps the final decision with my team. A Contributing findings section lists the specific scanner finding this issue was built from. The pull request description carries the same risk assessment, remediation summary, and proof from the console, so whoever reviews it in GitHub sees the evidence without leaving their workflow. The Findings tab lists the raw scanner findings across the environment, the evidence that issues are built from. The Scans tab shows the history of each scan with its status, origin, and request and completion times, and I use Configure scan frequency to change the cadence or Queue scan to run one on demand. The Configuration tab is where I manage the environment: the code and context sources it reads from, its code integrations, environment settings such as whether Continuum creates remediation patches, and the AWS collectors it uses for AWS context. In a single workflow, I work through the validated issues in priority order with each scan, reviewing the evidence and scope behind each one before I approve and merge the fixes I trust. Every fix waits for my approval, so the backlog keeps shrinking while my team keeps control of what ships. Now available AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is available today in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) Regions. For pricing, visit the pricing page . To learn more, visit the AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities product page and the User Guide . Give it a try in the AWS Continuum console today, and send us feedback through your usual AWS Support contacts. — Esra

title: Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime
body:
Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime | Bank of England – the UK's central bank Our use of cookies We use necessary cookies to make our site work. We’d also like to use some non-essential cookies (including third-party cookies) to help us improve the site. By clicking ‘Accept recommended settings’ on this banner, you accept our use of analytics cookies.   For more information on how these cookies work please see our Cookie policy . Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Regulators unveil plans to simplify Senior Manager and Certification Regime The number of financial services roles required to face enhanced checks from regulators will fall significantly under proposals that will support growth. Published on  
        22 October 2026 News release The number of financial services roles required to face enhanced checks from regulators will fall significantly under proposals that will support growth. The changes are expected to save firms around £2 billion over a 10-year period. The Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) have today announced parallel consultations on proposals to significantly streamline the Senior Managers and Certification regime (SM&CR). The SM&CR was introduced 10 years ago to instil a culture of accountability among senior decision-makers in regulated firms. Under the proposals, unnecessary burdens will be removed while high standards of individual accountability and conduct will remain unchanged, including the regulators’ commitment to ensuring that individuals are accountable for misconduct that affects society as well as their employers. The changes will allow firms to focus more resources to ensure good customer and market outcomes, recruit and appoint talent, and prioritise innovation and investment, all supporting UK growth and competitiveness. The key changes to the regime include: Regulator pre-approval will be removed for a range of regulatory functions, including Chief Actuaries and Chairs of Risk and Audit Committees. Firms will instead notify regulators of these appointments directly, gaining speed and flexibility while remaining responsible for ensuring candidates are fit and proper. Removing the Certification Regime and associated administrative requirements for around 139,000 individuals below senior manager level to be subject to annual certification checks and appear on the Financial Services Register. Raising the conduct rule breach reporting threshold for most staff below senior manager level and streamlining Conduct Rule training requirements. This enables firms to better target more serious misconduct. Certain Senior Manager roles, such as CEOs, CFOs and Chairs, will continue to require regulator pre-approval, including fit and proper tests, before appointment. Regulators will also be able to require pre-approval for otherwise notified roles in high-risk cases. Firms will remain responsible for ensuring their employees remain competent, suitable and meet appropriate standards of conduct, and those no longer requiring pre-approval will continue to be held to the same level of accountability as before. Katharine Braddick, Deputy Governor for Prudential Regulation and Chief Executive Officer of the PRA, said: “The Senior Managers Regime is an essential part of the UK’s regulatory framework. These proposals keep checks in place for the most important roles, meaning individuals are accountable for their actions, but reduce the administrative burden where it isn’t needed, giving firms more time to invest in growth-focused activities and greater flexibility in onboarding senior talent.” Sarah Pritchard, Deputy CEO, said: “SM&CR has delivered significant improvements in accountability and governance across financial services. We remain committed to ensuring individual accountability and good standards of behaviour across financial services. But we can achieve the same impact with a more streamlined regime, supporting our aim to be a smarter regulator.” Some of the proposed reforms require legislative change. By consulting now, the FCA and PRA will be ready to implement reforms quickly once legislation is passed. The consultations are now open until 22 January, seeking views on how the regime can be made more proportionate while maintaining high standards of individual accountability and conduct. The consultations invite feedback on all aspects of the proposals with policy expected to follow in 2027. This was announced as part of Mansion House speeches delivered by Katharine Braddick and Nikhil Rathi. In her speech, Katharine unveiled a five-year strategy for the PRA designed to transform the regulator, focusing on the resilience of the financial sector, the regulator’s growth and competitiveness objective, innovating with data and technology and boosting transparency. Notes to editors Read and engage with the PRA’s consultation . Read and respond to the FCA's consultation , and review the accompanying cost-benefit analysis. These consultations are the second and most significant phase of SM&CR reform. They build on changes in April 2026 , including longer timelines for senior manager applications following unexpected or temporary changes, removal of duplicate certification requirements for overlapping functions, and a 30% increase in enhanced firm thresholds for larger firms. The reforms are expected to reduce PRA SM&CR pre-approvals by 43% and halve the overall burden of the PRA regime. For FCA Enhanced solo-regulated firms where fewer SMFs apply, around 15% of applications would move to notification and 2 SMF roles would be removed, saving a further 19%. The PRA’s latest quarterly data shows that 98% of applications were determined within the proposed new two-month statutory deadline, compared with 98.3% in the FCA’s most recent quarterly metrics. The proposals build on wider PRA and FCA initiatives to support growth and competitiveness, including reforms to the ring-fencing regime to enable more flexible sharing of operational resources, proposals to index over 100 PRA thresholds to nominal GDP growth, and FCA reforms to strengthen the attractiveness of UK capital markets and support investment, and joint PRA/FCA initiatives to help innovative firms start up, scale up and compete internationally. title: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories
body: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories New AIOps platform connects infrastructure and workload telemetry to help operators increase uptime and maximize AI factory yield. October 22, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight. AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load. The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads. With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs. It analyzes billions of data points per hour using supervised and unsupervised machine learning. It learns normal behavior, detects previously unseen anomalies, predicts emerging failures and correlates related events based on the factory’s topology. Instead of sending every symptom to an operator, it can group an event storm into a focused incident with a likely root cause. Minerva comes with a native AI assistant and connects to external agentic AI tools. This adds a natural-language interface grounded in live telemetry. Operators can investigate cluster health and receive recommended remediation through conversation. Teams can keep a person in the loop to manually implement fixes or connect Minerva to automation through infrastructure application programming interfaces and external systems. Results That Maximize AI Factory Yield The ability to correlate workload and infrastructure issues along with its agentic AI capabilities help simplify AI factory operations. Instead of dealing with a blizzard of alerts, Minerva aggregates related problems into a single actionable item. This allows AIOps teams to move from reactive to proactive maintenance. And all of this helps AI factories maximize GPU uptime. Minerva delivers value for the key metrics AI factories focus on: Longer time between interruptions : Minerva spots trouble before it happens, so jobs run longer without incident. Faster time to repair : When an incident does happen, Minerva pinpoints the problem, leading to a significantly quicker resolution. Greater insight : Modern AI infrastructure generates a flood of data; Minerva filters it out, leaving only the handful of alerts that actually matter. IREN is among the NVIDIA partners using Minerva to optimize its AI factories. “As we scale our AI factories, the key to providing the best service for our customers is maximizing the productivity of our GPUs,” said Denis Skrinnikoff, chief technology officer of IREN. “NVIDIA Minerva gives our operations team one view across the network, the GPUs and the jobs running on them, so we focus more on proactive maintenance rather than troubleshooting. That visibility strengthens our operating model for the infrastructure we’re building next.” Joining IREN , Aolani , Bitdeer AI , IBM , Jio, Lambda , Quake AI and Tesla plan to deploy Minerva. In addition to Dell Technologies , Lenovo and Supermicro will offer Minerva as part of their AI factory operations portfolios. Learn more about NVIDIA Minerva . See notice regarding software product information. title: Cloud Deployment Incoming: ‘Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’ Arrives on GeForce NOW
body: Cloud Deployment Incoming: ‘Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’ Arrives on GeForce NOW Get memberships through Amazon on Fire TV, rally a party in ‘FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE’ and explore Season Two of ‘The Elder Scrolls Online.’ October 22, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Lock in and load out this GFN Thursday. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives on GeForce NOW at launch, bringing a new campaign, multiplayer action and DMZ, high-stakes extraction mode to supported devices . The campaign also gets an enhanced look: GeForce RTX 5080-class performance arrives for Ultimate members, bringing support for ray-tracing features in the cloud. There’s a new way to join the cloud, too: Existing supported Fire TV Stick users can now purchase one-month Performance or Ultimate memberships directly through Amazon, making it easier to sign up and start streaming on the big screen. Plus, Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE brings cinematic pixel art and strategic battles to the cloud, and The Elder Scrolls Online’s Echoes of Skyrim Season adds the entire Greymoor Chapter free for all ESO Standard Edition owners. It’s all part of six games joining the GeForce NOW library this week. Deployment Without the Downloads Squad up and answer the call on the cloud. Activision and Infinity Ward’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches today on GeForce NOW. Members can drop into the trenches in Korea, close-quarter combat in New York, high-octane chases through Paris, night raids in Mumbai and city-wide engagements to reclaim occupied territory. Fight as Private Park, a young South Korean soldier facing live combat for the first time alongside his squad as a routine patrol turns into a desperate fight for survival. Beyond the front lines, operator-turned-outlaw Captain Price is operating outside the system he once served, pursuing revenge through covert missions as the conflict spreads. Multiplayer pairs precise combat with fluid movement, a dozen core 6v6 maps from around the world and battlegrounds that are shaped by the campaign’s global conflict. The DMZ extraction mode sends players into contested territory to recover valuable technology, weigh objectives and decide when to get out. Loot, fight, negotiate, betray and extract — it’s all fair in the cloud and battleground. Ultimate members can now experience the campaign with ray tracing, powered by newly added GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, handhelds, mobile devices, browsers, supported TVs and more. With game downloads and installs handled by GeForce NOW, members can spend less time preparing a local rig and more time preparing the next loadout. Members can stream supported PC games they already own or purchase new titles from digital stores including Steam, Epic Games Store, Ubisoft Connect, Xbox PC Game Pass, GOG and EA. No downloads, installs, patches or updates stand between a new game and playtime. An Amazon Fire TV Stick, the GeForce NOW app and an Ultimate membership are all it takes to level up the living room with GeForce RTX 5080-powered gaming. A Pixel-Perfect Fantasy Classic roots. A new adventure. Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE launches today on GeForce NOW, bringing the series’ classic roots into a cinematic pixel-art world. Travel with companions bound by fate and uncover the truth behind a force threatening to bring everything to ruin. Strengthen the party with Visions of beloved FINAL FANTASY characters, each bringing unique skills and abilities to battle. Dynamic camera angles and pixelized 3D models give familiar fantasy a fresh perspective. Exploit enemy weaknesses to stagger foes, break their defenses and seize extra turns before finishing the bonus phase with powerful Resonance attacks. Airships, crystals, espers and moogles bring familiar series favorites to a world filled with secrets to discover. GeForce NOW handles the game’s downloads and storage in the cloud, leaving more space on supported devices for everyday essentials. Save the inventory management for potions and Phoenix Downs. Step Into a New Season in Tamriel Familiar lands. Fresh reasons to return. The Elder Scrolls Online ’s second season , Echoes of Skyrim , launched Wednesday, Oct. 21, free for all ESO players and ready to stream through GeForce NOW. Season Two gives everyone who owns ESO Standard Edition access to its Skyrim content and the Antiquities treasure-hunting system. The Markarth downloadable content follows Monday, Nov. 9, rounding out the additions with two classic zones to explore. The Season also introduces Solo Dungeons, reimagining challenges previously designed for groups. Moon Hunter Keep and March of Sacrifices have been redesigned and rebalanced for players ready to tackle their dangers alone. Earn new rewards and take on new challenges at your own pace without needing to find a group. A new Tamriel Tome also launched Oct. 21, offering both free and premium battle pass reward tracks. In addition, members can look for the following titles joining the GeForce NOW library this week: We Were Here Tomorrow (New release on Steam , Oct. 20) FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (New release on Steam , Oct. 22) Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (New release on Oct 23, available in the Call of Duty app) CONTROL Resonant ( Epic Game Store ) Crimson Desert ( Epic Games Store ) Planet Zoo 2 ( Xbox app , supports XBOX Play Anywhere) Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles. Gamers who want to test out high-performance GeForce NOW cloud gaming can start with a day pass to try premium cloud gaming before committing to a membership. Better yet, the cost of the day pass can be applied toward a first monthly membership — making it easy to try GeForce RTX-powered cloud gaming with the latest releases, then level up for more. title: The Trump Administration is Making Homeownership More Affordable
body: October 22, 2026 Proposed Rules Implement the ROAD to Housing Act and Support Affordable Homeownership in America WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury issued proposed regulations to make homeownership more affordable for hardworking Americans. The proposed regulations implement Section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (ROAD to Housing Act), which restricts large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, codifying key requirements of President Trump’s Executive Order 14376 , Stopping Wall Street from Competing with Main Street Homebuyers . “Under President Trump, this Administration continues to restore the path to affordable homeownership for millions of young and working families,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Treasury is working to ensure American families and workers have a fair shot at purchasing homes in their communities by increasing housing supply and limiting large institutional investors’ role in the market, while supporting a strong, stable housing market and avoiding unnecessary disruption.” RESTORING THE AMERICAN DREAM OF HOMEOWNERSHIP Beginning on January 7, 2027, a large institutional investor generally may not purchase, or enter into a contract to purchase, a single-family home unless the purchase qualifies as an “excepted purchase” under the ROAD to Housing Act. The ROAD to Housing Act defines a large institutional investor by reference to, among other things, whether an entity is engaged in the business of investing in, owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes and has direct or indirect investment control over at least 350 such homes. The ROAD to Housing Act permits several categories of excepted purchases, including purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs, renovate-to-rent programs, homeownership programs, and programs to boost homeownership. Today’s NPRM sets forth Treasury’s proposed framework to: Establish standards for purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs that promote continued investment in new housing; Provide a safe harbor for purchases made pursuant to renovate-to-rent programs that bring neglected homes back into the housing supply and up to code; Clarify the requirements for homeownership programs and programs to boost homeownership, including providing safe harbors for large institutional investors that provide meaningful financial support towards their renters’ purchase of a home; Clarify that an entity is engaged “in the business of” investing in , owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes when it does so for the purpose of receiving income or financial gain, and not incidentally to a different business; Define when an entity may qualify as a passive investor in another entity that owns a home because it does not share directors or officers with the other entity and does not have a property control right over the underlying homes; Clarify certain purchases involving debts previously contracted, loss mitigation, and transfers between large institutional investors that protect the liquidity of the housing market; and Clarify the calculation of the maximum civil penalty where a single prohibited purchase involves more than one large institutional investor. The proposed rule would provide non-exclusive safe harbors for several statutory requirements. These include standards for determining whether a home has been substantially rehabilitated under a renovate-to-rent program, whether a renter has received meaningful financial support under certain homeownership programs, and whether a renter has received a right of first refusal and 30-day first-look period. Treasury’s proposed approach recognizes that housing-market participants use a variety of ownership, investment, construction, servicing, and property-management structures and seeks to provide clarity without unnecessary disruption to housing supply, homebuilding, rehabilitation activity, or capital formation. Members of the public should submit comments in response to the NPRM within 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. The proposed regulations are available here . ###

title: Jury finds two Missoula men guilty of trafficking meth as part of multistate drug ring
body: Press Release Jury finds two Missoula men guilty of trafficking meth as part of multistate drug ring Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana MISSOULA – Two Missoula men who were accused of trafficking methamphetamine as part of a multistate drug ring were found guilty by a federal jury today, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Steger Smith said. Following a four-day trial, Arthur Ray Peoples, 69, and Joseph Frederick Ployhar, 45, were found guilty of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine, possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, and distribution of methamphetamine. The two men each face 15 years to life of prison, a $20 million fine and at least 10 years of supervised release. Their mandatory minimum sentences are increased because each has a prior conviction for a serious drug felony. U.S. District Judge William W. Mercer presided and will determine a sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Peoples and Ployhar were detained pending further proceedings. The government alleged in court documents and at trial that an investigation of a multistate drug ring identified Peoples as one of multiple meth dealers in Montana. Law enforcement used a confidential informant who bought roughly 27 grams of meth from Peoples on Jan. 28, 2025. Following the buy, investigators put Peoples under surveillance and then pulled him over when they suspected a drug deal was about to happen. In his vehicle, officers found several small baggies containing meth. From there, they searched his motel room and found more meth, digital scales, baggies, and ledgers. Ployhar was similarly identified through the course of the drug ring investigation. He was pulled over returning from Washington with another defendant, Jamie Maki . Investigators searched the vehicle and found roughly two and a half pounds of meth. Maki pleaded guilty earlier this year to drug trafficking charges and will be sentenced on Feb. 4, 2027. The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted the case. The Missoula Drug Task Force conducted the investigation. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. Contact Keri Leggett Acting Public Affairs Officer keri.leggett@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Neighborhoods Component USAO - Montana Press Release Number: 26-274

title: Convicted Firearms Trafficker Indicted for Possessing Firearms and Ammunition
body: Press Release Convicted Firearms Trafficker Indicted for Possessing Firearms and Ammunition Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant committed the alleged criminal conduct weeks after being released from federal prison BOSTON – A convicted firearms trafficker from Revere has been indicted by a federal grand jury for being a felon in possession of firearms. Cory Daigle, 31, of Revere, was indicted on charges of being a felon in possession of firearms and ammunition. The defendant will be arraigned at a later date. In August 2024 , Daigle was convicted of unlawfully trafficking in firearms, possessing a machinegun, receiving or possessing an unregistered firearm and additional firearms-related offenses. Daigle was sentenced to approximately two years in prison in that case and, according to court documents, had only been released from Bureau of Prisons custody a few weeks before he was allegedly found to possess 11 firearms, more than 100 rounds of ammunition and additional firearm components during a search of his residence on June 25, 2026. The charge of being a felon in possession of firearms and ammunition provides for a sentence of up to 15 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; and Justin Page, Acting Inspector in Charge of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service’s Boston Division made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, Boston Field Division and the Revere and Boston Police Departments. Assistant U.S. Attorney Julissa Walsh of the Major Crimes Unit is prosecuting the case. The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: High‑Speed Pursuit, Crash into Police Cruiser, Unlawful Possession of Loaded Glock, Yield a 28-Month Sentence for D.C. Felon
body: Press Release High‑Speed Pursuit, Crash into Police Cruiser, Unlawful Possession of Loaded Glock, Yield a 28-Month Sentence for D.C. Felon Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON - Trevon Troxler, 31, a previously convicted felon residing in the District, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 28 months incarceration in connection with a high‑speed flight from law enforcement that resulted in a collision with a federal police cruiser and the recovery of a loaded Glock 29 pistol, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Troxler pleaded guilty on May 13, 2026, before U.S. District Judge Amy Berman Jackson to unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition by a felon, and to destruction of federal property. In addition to the 28‑month prison term, Judge Berman Jackson ordered Troxler to serve three years of supervised release. Federal prosecutors had requested a 33‑month prison term. According to court documents, on Oct. 12, 2025, about 8:20 p.m., Troxler fled from law enforcement after officers attempted to stop the white Honda Accord he was driving in the 3500 block of Ames Street NE. Troxler led MPD officers and a Diplomatic Security Service agent through multiple sections of the city at high speed, striking a federal police cruiser and an uninvolved Hyundai. The collision with the Hyundai sent the car off the roadway and into a residence on the 1600 block of Eastern Avenue NE. After the collision, Troxler continued to flee in the Honda, traveling northbound on I-295, where he swerved in and out of traffic at a high rate of speed. As Troxler entered the ramp to Route 50, the Honda hit the federal police cruiser again. The Honda approached 33rd Place Northeast, and it struck a median in the roadway and stopped. Troxler opened the vehicle door, exited the vehicle, and fled on foot. Police quickly apprehended him at 2300 South Dakota Ave. NE. Officers recovered a loaded firearm from the driver’s side of Troxler’s vehicle. The weapon was a Glock 29 equipped with a laser attachment and loaded with one round in the chamber and 26 rounds in a high‑capacity magazine. Troxler caused more than $4,000 in damage to the federal police cruiser, which was property of the United States. Troxler has a previous conviction for unauthorized use of a vehicle and receiving stolen property, and another felony conviction for attempted assault with a dangerous weapon and unlawful possession of a firearm (crime of violence). The investigation was conducted by the Metropolitan Police Department, the Diplomatic Security Service, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives - Washington Field Office. The matter was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Emory V. Cole of the Federal Major Crimes Section under the President’s Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful Again initiative, which targets violent crime by prioritizing federal prosecution of armed repeat offenders and removing illegal firearms from District neighborhoods. 25cr242 Follow us on X , Instagram , and YouTube Or at https://www.justice.gov/usao-dc Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - District of Columbia

title: Gang Member Pleads Guilty to Federal Gun and Drug Charges
body: Press Release Gang Member Pleads Guilty to Federal Gun and Drug Charges Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant manufactured and sold firearms, silencers and machinegun conversion devices; distributed controlled substances; and committed an armed home invasion while on state parole for armed robberies BOSTON – A Vice Lord gang member from Athol, Mass. has pleaded guilty in federal court in Boston to gun and drug charges. At the time of the offenses the defendant was on parole following multiple six- to 10-year concurrent state prison sentences. Keith Harlow, a/k/a “Lord Savage,” 40, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to distribute controlled substances; being a felon in possession of firearm and ammunition; conspiracy to interfere with commerce by robbery; and engaging in the business of manufacturing and dealing in firearms without a license. U.S. District Court Judge Indira Talwani scheduled sentencing for Jan. 12, 2027. Harlow was charged in May 2025, however he remained a fugitive until his arrest in August 2025 . Harlow is a member of a Vice Lords chapter known as the Four Corner Hustlers. Known by his street name “Lord Savage,” Harlow has been convicted of multiple prior armed robberies and, at the time of the offenses, was on parole following multiple six to 10-year concurrent state prison sentences. In 2025, while on state parole, Harlow sent numerous text messages and was captured in photographs and video recordings in possession of firearms, a suppressor and machinegun conversion device, commonly known as a selector “switch.” In numerous text messages, Harlow discussed the manufacturing of firearms and selector switches and the sale of numerous firearms he had in his possession. One of the firearms seized during the investigation was purchased by co-conspirator Andrew Poor and given to Harlow. Further investigation of Poor revealed his involvement in a January 2025 home invasion of a residence in Athol. Dante Machuca was also identified as participating in the home invasion, along with Harlow and Poor. According to the charging documents, Harlow, Poor and Machuca, entered into the residence of a suspected drug dealer armed with firearms in order to rob the dealer of drugs and proceeds. Harlow engaged in a struggle with the dealer and fired his weapon to demonstrate its authenticity, before putting the hot barrel of the firearm against the victim’s abdomen. At the time of this home invasion, Harlow was on parole for multiple state prison terms. During a search of Harlow’s residence on May 29, 2025, multiple firearm receivers, suspected firearm suppressors, machinegun conversion devices, 3D printers and firearm manufacturing supplies were recovered. Approximately 100 grams of suspected cocaine was also found in the residence. A review of Perry’s cellphone seized during his arrest on state charges on May 29, 2025, revealed that Harlow and Perry worked together to distribute controlled substances and sell firearms throughout Massachusetts. In text message communications, Harlow and Perry discussed committing multiple robberies and using firearms to shoot at various individuals. At the time of the offenses, Harlow and Perry were prohibited from possessing firearms due to numerous prior felony convictions, including Perry’s youthful offender conviction of manslaughter. At the time of all the messages, Harlow was on parole following multiple concurrent state prison sentences for multiple armed robberies and Perry was on probation for a domestic violence offense. Perry was sentenced in September 2026 to 97 months in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release. The charge of being a felon in possession of a firearm provides for a sentence of up to 15 years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of conspiring to distribute controlled substances provides for a sentence of up to 20 years, at least three years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $1 million. The charge of unlicensed manufacturing and dealing in firearms provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of conspiracy to interfere with commerce by robbery provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division; David E. Sullivan, Northwestern District Attorney; and Athol Police Chief Craig Lundgren made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the United States Marshal Service in Massachusetts; the U.S. Marshal’s Service in the Northern District of Georgia; United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia; the Massachusetts State Police; the Franklin County House of Correction; and the Massachusetts Department of Correction. Assistant U.S. Attorney Philip A. Mallard of the Organized Crime & Gang Unit is prosecuting the case. Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Federal Awards Bring Nearly $1.5 Million to Jefferson County During Domestic Violence Awareness Month
body: Press Release Federal Awards Bring Nearly $1.5 Million to Jefferson County During Domestic Violence Awareness Month Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Alabama BIRMINGHAM, Ala. – As the Department of Justice and communities across the country observe Domestic Violence Awareness Month this October, new federal awards totaling nearly $1.5 million are coming to two of Jefferson County’s key partners in the fight against domestic violence: the Jefferson County District Attorney’s Office and One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center. The Department of Justice’s Office on Violence Against Women (OVW) has awarded $750,000 through its Improving Criminal Justice Responses program to Jefferson County, on behalf of the Jefferson County District Attorney’s Office. Authorized by the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA), the program supports partnerships among governments, courts, and victim-service providers to treat domestic violence as the serious crime it is and to seek safety and autonomy for victims. The funding will expand and strengthen the investigation and prosecution of domestic violence cases, while providing additional support to victims seeking protection and justice. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Administration for Children and Families’ Family and Youth Services Bureau, has awarded $358,333 to One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center for the first year of a two-year project beginning September 30, 2026, with the same amount anticipated for the second year, for a total of $716,666. Funded through the Family Violence Prevention and Services Act, the award will support counseling and advocacy for survivors and their children, and growth of One Place’s work through Camp HOPE America. Camp HOPE is a national, year-round program for children ages 7 to 17 affected by domestic and family violence. One Place hosts Alabama’s only Camp HOPE America site. “Domestic violence is not an issue of anger management. It is an issue of power and control, and many of its deaths are predictable and preventable when a community responds together,” said Rebecca McWilliams, Executive Director of One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center. “Thanks to the Violence Against Women Act and the partnerships we have built with local and federal law enforcement, we have come a long way, and we still have a long way to go. This support from the Department of Health and Human Services will help us walk alongside survivors and make sure children who have witnessed violence have somewhere to belong.” The new resources build on results already visible in Jefferson County. In 2023, the county recorded 25 statutory domestic violence homicides. As of mid-September 2026, it has recorded two, and Birmingham has recorded none. “October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and the message from this office is simple: domestic violence is a violent crime, and it will not be tolerated in the Northern District of Alabama,” said U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr. “Victims deserve safety, dignity, and justice. These awards put real resources behind the prosecutors who hold abusers accountable and the advocates who walk beside survivors and their children. When we stand together, from the streets to the courtroom, offenders are held accountable and families get the help they need. This is a united front, and my office will keep championing our partners’ work in Washington.” The awards also support Operation Safe Families, the U.S. Attorney’s Office initiative that brings together federal law enforcement, state and local law enforcement, prosecutors, and victim-service providers. Because abusers with access to firearms pose a significant and often deadly risk, the U.S. Attorney’s Office is committed to prosecuting federal cases against abusers who are prohibited from possessing firearms. Operation Safe Families is part of the office’s Project Safe Neighborhoods strategy, because offenders who terrorize their intimate partners often go on to commit other violent crimes and pose extreme risks to law enforcement officers. Nearly one-half of all offenders federally prosecuted by the Northern District of Alabama for violent offenses have a history of domestic violence. Since 2024, the Northern District of Alabama has indicted 62 domestic violence offenders across fourteen counties for various federal offenses. “Domestic violence is one of the clearest warning signs for deadly violence in our community. Roughly 70% of identified homicide offenders in Jefferson County have a history of it, and our office prosecutes more of these cases than homicides, attempted murders, and robberies combined,” said District Attorney Danny Carr. “When police, prosecutors, courts, and advocates work together before a crisis turns fatal, lives are saved. These resources help us sustain that work, and our goal must be zero. I appreciate our federal partners for standing with us.” To learn more about One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center or Camp HOPE, please visit One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center . If you need help: If you are in immediate danger, call 911. The National Domestic Violence Hotline is available at 1-800-799-SAFE (7233), 1-800-787-3224 (TTY), or TheHotline.org . One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center can be reached during business hours at 205-453-7261. Additional national, state, and local resources are listed at Justice.gov/OVW/Resources-Victims-and-Survivors . Updated October 22, 2026 Component USAO - Alabama, Northern

title: Meriden Tax Preparer Charged with Tax Fraud Offenses
body: Press Release Meriden Tax Preparer Charged with Tax Fraud Offenses Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of IRS Criminal Investigation in New England, today announced that YURIDIA TRUJILLO, 43, of Meriden, has been charged by indictment with preparing numerous false income tax returns. As alleged in the indictment, Trujillo operated as a tax return preparer under the business name Yuri’s LLC.  For the 2017 through 2024 tax years, Trujillo prepared at least 4,335 tax returns for clients.  On many of her clients’ tax returns, Trujillo made materially false entries, including false deductions for Individual Retirement Account (“IRA”) contributions and child and dependent care expenses; fabricated businesses and business deductions; fictitious losses for the buying and selling of stocks and cryptocurrency that clients never owned; and fabricated rental properties that would report little to no rental income, but significant deductible rental expenses. The indictment further alleges that in association with preparing and filing Forms 1040 for clients, Trujillo also filed Forms 8888, entitled “Allocation of Refund,” which allow taxpayers to elect to have a portion of a direct deposit tax refund deposited into up to three different bank accounts.  Trujillo filed false Forms 8888 in connection with client tax returns that included the bank account and routing numbers of her own bank account and the bank account of an associate, thereby diverting a portion of client refunds to herself. On October 7, 2026, a grand jury in New Haven returned an indictment charging Trujillo with 19 counts of aiding and assisting in the preparation and presentation of a false income tax return, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of three years on each count. Trujillo was arrested on October 9, 2026, and is released on a $50,000 bond pending trial. U.S. Attorney Sullivan stressed that an indictment is not evidence of guilt.  Charges are only allegations, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This investigation is being conducted by the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division.  The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul A. Riley. Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Tax Component USAO - Connecticut

title: Six Aliens Charged for Falsely Claiming United States’ Citizenship to Vote and/or Illegally Voting in 2022 and 2024 Elections
body: Press Release Six Aliens Charged for Falsely Claiming United States’ Citizenship to Vote and/or Illegally Voting in 2022 and 2024 Elections Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Ocala, Florida – United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe announces the filing of federal charges involving six aliens, all lawful permanent residents, for falsely claiming United States’ citizenship to vote and/or illegally voting in 2022 and 2024 elections. Jamie Orlando Sosa Sardina, 60, a Cuban national, Martha Haydee Desantis, 81, an Ecuadorian national, and Lise Marie Johnson, 69, a Canadian national, have each been charged by indictment with making a false statement claiming United States’ citizenship to vote and illegal voting by an alien. If convicted, each faces a maximum penalty of five years in federal prison on the false statement charge and up to one year imprisonment for the illegal voting offense. According to the indictments, Sardina registered to vote in 2022 and voted in the 2022 and 2024 federal general elections; Desantis re-registered to vote in 2024 and voted in the 2022 and 2024 federal general elections; and Johnson registered to vote in 2021 and voted in the 2022 federal general election. All voted despite knowing that they were not citizens of the United States. Luis Manuel Perez, 72, a Cuban national, Diane Wendy Curley, 55, a Canadian national, and Pedro Igor A. Franco, 37, a Brazilian national, all lawful permanent residents, were charged by information with illegal voting by an alien. If convicted, each faces a maximum penalty of up to one year in federal prison. According to the informations, Perez and Curley voted in the 2022 and 2024 federal general elections; Franco voted in the 2024 federal general election. Indictments and informations are merely formal charging documents alleging that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law. Every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until proven guilty. These cases were investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, the Florida Department of State - Office of Election Crimes, and the Hernando County Supervisor of Elections. They are being prosecuted by Special Assistant United States Attorney Jerry M. Harre. Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: U.S. Attorney Moore Capito Joins with Law Enforcement Partners to Promote the DEA’s 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24, 2026
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney Moore Capito Joins with Law Enforcement Partners to Promote the DEA’s 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24, 2026 Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of West Virginia CHARLESTON, W.Va. – United States Attorney Moore Capito is encouraging West Virginians to safely dispose of unwanted medications on Saturday, October 24, 2026, the Drug Enforcement Administration’s 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day. From 10 a.m. to 2 p.m ., DEA and law enforcement partners will collect tablets, capsules, patches, and other solid forms of prescription drugs at more than 65 sites throughout the state, including more than three dozen locations in the Southern District of West Virginia. A collection site locator is available at www.DEATakeBack.com . All sites will accept old, unwanted, and expired prescription medications for free and anonymous disposal. “Drug Take Back Day is a critical opportunity to anonymously remove dangerous, unused prescription drugs from our homes before they end up in the wrong hands,” Capito said. “Law enforcement is sounding the alarm: every pill not turned in is a risk to our community. By acting now, we can stop misuse before it starts and keep these drugs off our streets. Your quick, anonymous action today can help save lives.” Collection sites will not accept syringes, sharps, and illicit drugs. Liquid products, such as cough syrup, should remain sealed in their original container. The cap must be tightly sealed to prevent leakage. In partnership with local law enforcement, Take Back Day has removed more than 20.4 million pounds (10,200 tons) of medication from circulation since its inception. The total includes 149,901 pounds collected in West Virginia, with 4,063 pounds of that disposed of during the previous Take Back Day on April 25, 2026. More information is available at www.DEATakeBack.com . A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia. ### Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Community Outreach Prescription Drugs Component USAO - West Virginia, Southern

title: Oklahoma City Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Possessing Machinegun Conversion Device
body: Press Release Oklahoma City Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Possessing Machinegun Conversion Device Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Oklahoma OKLAHOMA CITY – XZHAVIER LEE WALTON , 21, of Oklahoma City, has been sentenced to serve 18 months in federal prison for unlawful possession of a machinegun, announced U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester. According to public records, on February 19, 2026, officers with the Oklahoma City Police Department stopped a vehicle as part of an investigation into a robbery that had occurred earlier that day. During the traffic stop, officers detected the odor of marijuana and detained all occupants, including Walton, who was seated in the rear passenger area behind the driver’s seat. Underneath the driver’s seat, directly in front of Walton, officers recovered a handgun fitted with a machinegun conversion device (MCD), commonly known as a “switch.” When installed, MCDs convert semiautomatic weapons into fully automatic machineguns, and possession of MCDs violates federal law. Through their investigation, law enforcement determined that the handgun belonged to Walton. On March 3, 2026, a federal Grand Jury charged Walton with unlawful possession of a machinegun. Walton pleaded guilty on July 15, 2026, and admitted he knowingly possessed a handgun modified with an MCD. At a sentencing hearing on October 21, 2026, U.S. District Judge Charles Goodwin sentenced Walton to serve 18 months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release. This case is the result of an investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Oklahoma City Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney David Nichols, Jr., prosecuted the case. This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative to reduce violent crime through coordinated federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement partnerships. PSN is a key component of Operation Take Back America (OTBA), the Department’s nationwide effort to combat violent crime and other threats to public safety. This case is also part of “Project Switch Off,” the Western District of Oklahoma’s implementation of OTBA. “Project Switch Off” targets illegal machinegun conversion devices to address the significant danger these illegal devices present and to remove them from our streets. Reference is made to public filings for additional information. Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Oklahoma, Western

title: Montco Man, 20, Pleads Guilty to 2024 Carjacking in Which He Shot and Seriously Wounded the Victim
body: Press Release Montco Man, 20, Pleads Guilty to 2024 Carjacking in Which He Shot and Seriously Wounded the Victim Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Pennsylvania PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Niyaz Burgess, 20, of Elkins Park, Pennsylvania, entered a plea of guilty today before United States District Judge Kai N. Scott to carjacking and using, carrying, and discharging a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence. The defendant was charged by indictment in August of last year. As detailed in court filings and statements, on July 14, 2024, shortly before three in the morning, Burgess carjacked and shot a man on the 6600 block of Limekiln Pike in Philadelphia, driving away in the victim’s vehicle. The victim suffered two gunshot wounds to the abdomen and one to the arm, resulting in significant internal injuries. On July 15, 2024, around 4:30 a.m., Pennsylvania State Troopers found the victim’s crashed and abandoned car on I-95 South in Tinicum Township. They secured the vehicle and transferred it to the custody of the Philadelphia Police Department. Forensic testing subsequently revealed Burgess’s fingerprints and palm print on the stolen vehicle. The defendant is scheduled to be sentenced on February 15 and faces a maximum possible term of life imprisonment, five years of supervised release, and a fine of $500,000, with a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in prison. This case was investigated by the FBI Philadelphia Violent Crimes Task Force and the Philadelphia Police Department, with assistance from the Pennsylvania State Police, and is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Sandra Urban. Contact USAPAE.PressBox@usdoj.gov 215-861-8300 Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Pennsylvania, Eastern

title: Delaware Real-Estate Agent Agrees to Pay $80,000 to Resolve False-Claims-Act Allegations Involving HUD Home Purchase
body: Press Release Delaware Real-Estate Agent Agrees to Pay $80,000 to Resolve False-Claims-Act Allegations Involving HUD Home Purchase Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Delaware Nick.Young@usdoj.gov WILMINGTON, Del. – Lauren Janes, a licensed real-estate agent residing in Delaware, has agreed to pay $80,000 to resolve allegations that she violated the False Claims Act by falsely certifying to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) that she would live in a home she bought from the agency. HUD sells homes it acquires in foreclosure after homeowners default on Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loans. To expand affordable homeownership for low- and moderate-income buyers, HUD first offers these homes exclusively to owner-occupants, who must agree to live in the property as their primary residence for at least one year. Investors may bid only if no owner-occupant buyer comes forward. According to the settlement, Janes bid on a HUD-owned home on Bonwood Road in Wilmington, Delaware, during the owner-occupant period in December 2021. On December 15, 2021, she signed a HUD sales contract to buy the property for $110,000, checking the box identifying herself as an owner-occupant rather than an investor. In a purchase addendum, she certified that she would live in the home as her primary residence for at least 12 months. Janes never lived at the property. After taking ownership on January 14, 2022, she renovated the home and, less than six months later, agreed to sell it for $202,000. The sale closed on July 22, 2022. Under the agreement, Janes will pay $80,000 and has agreed to a 48-month voluntary exclusion from participating in federal procurement and non-procurement transactions, including any other purchases of HUD-owned properties. “Lauren Janes made false statements to HUD to skip the line and purchase a HUD-owned home before other investors could bid on it,” said U.S. Attorney Benjamin L. Wallace.  “My Office and its law-enforcement partners will not allow anyone to cheat federal programs, especially affordable-housing programs meant to protect American families.” “Lauren Janes used her mortgage industry expertise to exploit the FHA program, misrepresenting her home’s occupancy to secure more favorable financing for herself,” said Special Agent in Charge Shawn Rice with the U.S Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Inspector General (OIG). “As a licensed professional, she understood the program’s requirements yet chose personal gain over professional integrity. HUD OIG remains committed to working with our law-enforcement and prosecutorial partners to hold accountable those who abuse HUD programs and put taxpayer resources at risk.” Janes admitted the facts set out in the statement of facts attached to the settlement agreement at the end of this release. The matter was investigated by HUD Office of Inspector General.  The settlement was handled by Assistant U.S. Attorney Claudia L. Pare. The claims resolved by this settlement are allegations only, and there has been no determination of liability. janes_settlement_agreement.pdf Updated October 22, 2026 Component USAO - Delaware

title: Texas Mexican Mafia Member Sentenced to Over 20 Years in Federal Prison
body: Press Release Texas Mexican Mafia Member Sentenced to Over 20 Years in Federal Prison Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas SAN ANTONIO – A member of the Texas Mexican Mafia was sentenced in San Antonio today to 250 months in federal prison for drug trafficking and firearm offenses, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, David Cortez Jr. aka “Tazmanian” aka “Taz,” 35, of San Antonio, was a sergeant in the Texas Mexican Mafia. Through an investigation led by the Drug Enforcement Administration, Cortez was caught discussing the collection of narcotics proceeds for the Texas Mexican Mafia to make another multi-kilogram purchase of methamphetamine. Due to the investigation, agents were able to seize the narcotics before they could be distributed in the community. Cortez was arrested in October 2020 and was found in possession of heroin and a loaded handgun. He was indicted with 11 co-defendants on Sept. 30, 2020. With the exception of Rudy Arreola, who was indicted separately in 2021, all defendants in this case have been sentenced. Arreola is scheduled to be sentenced on Dec. 10. Donald Trevino, who served as the “free world” General of the Texas Mexican Mafia, was sentenced to 300 months in federal prison in October 2022. “As a ranking officer in one of the most notorious gangs in San Antonio, David Cortez Jr. and his many co-conspirators flooded our community with narcotics,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “I extend my gratitude to the DEA along with the FBI and our partners at the San Antonio Police Department for their efforts in safeguarding our community and protecting Americans. This office remains committed to dismantling the violent criminal organizations that interfere with our God-given rights to live our lives, enjoy liberty, and pursue happiness.” “Through aggressive and proactive investigative collaborations, DEA San Antonio Division saved lives by staying one step ahead of David Cortez Jr., dismantling his efforts to profit from the destruction of our communities,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge for the San Antonio Division, Miguel A. Madrigal. “His criminal enterprise has been brought to a halt, and he will now face the consequences of his actions for years to come.” “The FBI is committed to keeping dangerous, illegal drugs out of the communities we serve,” said FBI San Antonio Special Agent in Charge Daniel Faith. “This considerable sentencing puts those who would seek to harm others for their own gain on notice that justice will find you. Cortez will no longer pose a threat to the citizens of San Antonio because of our strong partnerships with DEA, SAPD and the U.S. Attorney's Office.” The DEA, FBI and San Antonio Police Department investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Eric Yuen prosecuted the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Western

title: Justice Department’s Civil Division and the Department of Health & Human Services Announce Anti-Fraud Healthcare Self-Disclosure Pilot Program
body: Press Release Justice Department’s Civil Division and the Department of Health & Human Services Announce Anti-Fraud Healthcare Self-Disclosure Pilot Program Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The Six-Month Pilot Program Provides a Pathway for Legitimate Healthcare Companies to Resolve Potential False Claims Act Violations The Department of Justice Civil Division has partnered with the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to launch a Healthcare False Claims Act Self-Disclosure Pilot Program (FCA SDPP), which is designed to give healthcare companies a way to quickly resolve past misconduct by self-disclosing potential violations of the federal False Claims Act (FCA) and to prioritize the government’s resources toward recalcitrant actors. This civil pilot program builds on longstanding Department principles, discussed further here and here , to promote predictable and efficient resolution of corporate misconduct while recovering damages and penalties for taxpayers. [1] “Voluntary self-disclosure is a powerful indicator of a company’s commitment to compliance and accountability,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “This pilot program offers a favorable resolution framework to companies that want to take responsibility for past conduct while allowing the Department to concentrate resources on those who deliberately exploit our healthcare system. But for companies unwilling to take accountability, the Civil Division, in partnership with whistleblowers, will root out the fraud.” “By providing predictable and clear incentives for self-disclosure, this pilot program offers responsible companies an opportunity to move forward as stronger partners to federal healthcare programs,” said Deputy Assistant Attorney General Brenna Jenny of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “When companies identify misconduct and take meaningful steps to fix the problem and repay the government plus penalties, the Department will take those actions into account in determining appropriate resolutions.” Participants must describe all relevant details relating to the disclosing company’s conduct that potentially violates the federal FCA and produce documents sufficient to fully reflect the nature, terms, and operation of the disclosed potential FCA violations. Self-disclosing companies must describe the remedial actions they have taken and make a financial repayment with a 1.25–1.6 multiplier. The multiplier applied will vary based on factors such as the timeliness of the self-disclosure, the duration and scope of the misconduct, the involvement of senior leadership, the financial benefit to the disclosing company, and whether the disclosing company has successor liability for the misconduct but promptly remediated. In exchange, companies will receive a coordinated civil release from liability under the federal False Claims Act and certain HHS administrative authorities. Companies may submit self-disclosures electronically to FCA-SDPP@usdoj.gov. The FCA SDPP will accept submissions through April 22, 2027. Late and incomplete submissions will not be reviewed. Note : A copy of the FCA SDPP protocol is available here . [1] The FCA SDPP is a pilot program available for conduct that potentially violates civil laws. A company seeking to self-disclose potential criminal conduct related to health care must disclose that conduct to the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division pursuant to the National Fraud Enforcement Division and HHS-OIG Policy on Coordination of Voluntary Self-Disclosure in Health Care Fraud Matters. A company that makes a voluntary self-disclosure of criminal matters to the Fraud Division within the meaning of the CEP need not make a duplicative submission to FCA-SDPP@usdoj.gov. Where a company also seeks a civil FCA release through the FCA SDPP, supplementation of its Fraud Division disclosure will be requested only to the extent necessary. Updated October 22, 2026 Topics False Claims Act Fraud Component Civil Division Press Release Number: 26-1218
