title: Massachusetts Man Convicted of Abusive Sexual Contact of a Minor Aboard Flight to Boston
body: Press Release Massachusetts Man Convicted of Abusive Sexual Contact of a Minor Aboard Flight to Boston Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant worked his hand in between the seat directly in front of him, where a minor victim was seated and touched the minor victim’s buttocks BOSTON – A Newton, Mass. man was convicted on Oct. 16, 2026 following a three-day jury trial, of making repeated sexual contact with a 17-year-old female passenger (minor victim) seated directly in front of him onboard a flight from Puerto Rico to Boston in August 2024. Jonathan Alan Lefman, 48, was convicted of one count of abusive sexual contact while in the special aircraft jurisdiction of the United States. U.S. District Court Judge Julia E. Kobick scheduled sentencing for Jan. 12, 2027. Lefman was arrested and charged by criminal complaint in February 2025 and later indicted by a federal grand jury in March 2025 . “The defendant repeatedly sexually abused a minor who was simply trying to travel safely aboard a commercial flight,” said United States Attorney Leah B. Foley. “No one should have to fear being sexually assaulted, whether in the air or on the ground. Today’s verdict holds the defendant accountable for his disturbing conduct and sends a clear message that those who prey on vulnerable passengers will face justice.” “This verdict delivers justice for a young teen who showed remarkable courage following an appalling act. No one should ever be subjected to such harmful and predatory conduct—least of all in a confined, public space where she was entitled to feel safe,” said Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division. “The FBI is fully committed to protecting children and ensuring those who exploit or abuse them, like Mr. Lefman, are brought to justice.” On Aug. 30, 2024, Lefman was a passenger onboard a JetBlue flight flying from San Juan, Puerto Rico to Boston with his wife and four children. On multiple occasions during the flight and while on the ground waiting to deplane in Boston, Lefman engaged in abusive sexual contact with the minor victim. Specifically, Lefman worked his hand in between the area between the back and bottom of the seat directly in front of him, where the minor victim was seated, and touched the minor victim’s buttocks without her permission. On at least one occasion when he did so, the minor victim saw Lefman’s reflection leaning between the seats in the seatback monitor in front of her. On the last occasion when he touched or attempted to touch her buttocks, the minor victim was able to use her cell phone camera to take a video of Lefman’s fingers protruding between the back and bottom of the minor victim’s seat. Upon exiting the aircraft, while still on the jet bridge, the minor victim took a video of Lefman as he got off the aircraft. After deplaning, the minor victim’s adult female family member who had been traveling in a different row reported Lefman’s conduct to a JetBlue supervisor and confronted Lefman, showing the video of his fingers to support her statement. The charge of abusive sexual contact while in the special aircraft jurisdiction of the United States provides for a sentence of up to two years in prison, five years to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. U.S. Attorney Foley, FBI SAC Docks and Colonel Geoffrey D. Noble, Superintendent of the Massachusetts State Police made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by Boston Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Elianna J. Nuzum and Julissa Walsh of the Criminal Division are prosecuting the case. Updated October 22, 2026 Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Foreign-Owned Industrial Manufacturing Company to Pay $1.5 Million to Settle False Claims Act Allegations Related to Paycheck Protection Program Loan
body: Press Release Foreign-Owned Industrial Manufacturing Company to Pay $1.5 Million to Settle False Claims Act Allegations Related to Paycheck Protection Program Loan Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Michigan DETROIT – United States Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon Jr. announced today that 3CON Corporation, a company located in Wixom, Michigan that designs and manufactures automated production systems for the automotive and life sciences industries, has agreed to pay $1,500,439.50 to settle allegations that it violated the False Claims Act by making false statements to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) to obtain a Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan for which 3CON was ineligible. Congress created the PPP in March 2020 to provide emergency financial assistance to American businesses suffering from the economic effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. Under the PPP, eligible small businesses could receive forgivable loans guaranteed by the SBA. Regulations provided various eligibility requirements for the PPP, including limitations on the number of employees and restrictions for foreign-owned companies.When applying for PPP loans, borrowers were required to certify the truthfulness and accuracy of all information provided in their loan applications. In January 2021, 3CON obtained a second draw PPP loan for $828,498. At the time of its loan application, 3CON shared common ownership with 3CON Anlagenbau GmbH, an Austrian Company. The United States alleged that 3CON falsely certified that it was eligible for the second draw loan and loan forgiveness, even though, together with its foreign affiliates, it had more than 300 employees, in violation of the PPP rules in effect at the time 3CON obtained the funds. This civil settlement resolved a sealed lawsuit originally filed under the qui tam or whistleblower provisions of the False Claims Act, which permit private parties to file suit on behalf of the United States for false claims and share in a portion of the government’s recovery. The qui tam lawsuit has been unsealed and is captioned U.S. ex rel. Verity Investigations, LLC v. 3CON Corporation , Case No. 2:25-cv-13896. The whistleblower will receive 10% of the settlement amount. This matter was handled by Assistant U.S. Attorney Bradley H. Darling from the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Michigan, with assistance from the SBA’s Office of General Counsel. Individuals with information about allegations of fraud involving COVID-19 are encouraged to report it by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud (NCDF) Hotline at 866-720-5721 or via the NCDF Web Complaint Form at: https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only; there has been no determination of liability. body: Press Release Federal Crackdown: 11 charged in North Texas for firearms trafficking, meth distribution and machine gun offenses Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas ABILENE, Texas – United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced today that federal charges have been filed against eleven individuals for various firearms and drug trafficking offenses following a Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives-led investigation and violent crimes reduction initiative in Abilene. All defendants are in federal custody and made their initial appearances today before U.S. Magistrate Judge John R. Parker. “Today, we delivered a decisive blow against the criminal networks that threaten Abilene and the broader Taylor County community through the trafficking of illegal firearms and the distribution of dangerous narcotics,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “As Abilene continues to grow, protecting the safety and stability of this city remains one of my highest priorities. Let this serve as a clear warning: In unwavering partnership with our federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies, my office will relentlessly pursue and dismantle these organizations. We will not allow our streets to be undermined by gangs, firearm traffickers, and drug dealers, particularly when these crimes fuel the brutal operations of cartel driven crime.” “Those who traffic firearms to criminals, arm cartel-connected networks, and push meth into our communities are fueling violent crime,” ATF Dallas Special Agent in Charge Brian Garner. “ATF and our partners are disrupting these operations, targeting the people behind them, and holding them accountable. We will not stop pursuing those who threaten public safety.” Firearms Trafficking and Related Offenses Seven individuals face charges related to firearms trafficking, including sales to prohibited persons and conspiracy to transfer firearms for use in felony and drug trafficking crimes, some with alleged ties to Mexican cartels: Larry Don Knight, Kenneth Dwayne Tittle and Dylan Tyler Todd are charged in a criminal complaint with conspiracy and attempt to transfer firearms for use in felony and drug trafficking crimes, possession of firearms by convicted felons, attempted sale of firearms to prohibited persons, and distribution and possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance (methamphetamine). According to court documents, these individuals allegedly trafficked firearms and methamphetamine in the Abilene area, with some firearms intended for Mexican cartels. Defendants Tittle and Todd, both convicted felons, are also charged with selling firearms to a known prohibited person. Knight is additionally charged with methamphetamine distribution. Randall Kent Whitaker and Brandi Michelle Whitaker are charged with conspiracy to transfer a firearm for use in a felony and drug trafficking crimes, and attempted sale or transfer of a firearm to a prohibited person. The complaint alleges that the duo trafficked firearms in Abilene, including sales to a known felon, with the understanding that the firearms were bound for Mexican cartels. Whitaker is a convicted felon. Josiah Haynesworth is charged with sale or transfer of a firearm to a prohibited person and trafficking in firearms. Court documents allege Haynesworth knowingly sold a firearm to a convicted felon in Abilene. Justine Aten Harris is charged with possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. According to court documents, Harris allegedly sold multiple firearms, including a Springfield Armory .45 pistol and a 12-gauge shotgun, to a confidential informant in September 2026. Methamphetamine Trafficking Three individuals are facing federal charges for their alleged roles in a methamphetamine trafficking conspiracy: Coby Dale Foust, Jesseca Denah Foust and Christal Louise Rule are charged with conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine. According to the complaint, these defendants allegedly trafficked significant quantities of methamphetamine in the greater Abilene, Anson, and Albany areas of Texas. Illegal Machine Gun Possession One individual is charged with illegal possession of a machine gun: Aiden Ochoa is charged with illegal possession of a machine gun. The complaint alleges that Mr. Ochoa possessed a handgun equipped with an illegal machine gun conversion device, commonly known as a "Glock switch," in Abilene. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Dallas Division and the Abilene Police Department conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew L. Tusing and Jordan Magee from the Abilene Division are prosecuting the cases. A criminal complaint is merely an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. title: Four Men Charged with Pandemic Relief Fraud
body: Press Release Four Men Charged with Pandemic Relief Fraud Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts One defendant allegedly spent pandemic relief funds at casino BOSTON – Four individuals have been charged for allegedly defrauding the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program by submitting fraudulent applications. The following individuals have been indicted on one count each of wire fraud: Jonathan Arroyo, 43, of Boston; Daquan Dooley, 37, of Attleboro; Demetrous Thomas, 36, of Acushnet; and Gianni Williams Johnson, 28, of Boston. Arroyo, Dooley and Thomas were arrested and appeared in federal court in Boston. Williams Johnson is currently detained on an unrelated matter in Suffolk Superior Court and will appear in federal court in Boston on a later date. According to the charging documents, Arroyo, Thomas and Williams Johnson allegedly submitted fraudulent PPP applications on behalf of themselves, claiming that they owned businesses that suffered economic harm because of the COVID-19 pandemic. They each submitted fraudulent tax return information to justify their applications. They were each awarded forgivable PPP loans in the amount of over $20,000. In fact, it is alleged that none of these individuals owned businesses and their fraudulent tax return information was never filed with the IRS. It is alleged that bank records show that none of these individuals used the loans for payroll expenses. According to the charging documents, Dooley also allegedly submitted a fraudulent EIDL application on behalf of himself, claiming that he owned a business that suffered economic harm because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Dooley claimed that he would use the loan for business expenses, such as payroll and rent. After Dooley’s application, he was given a $10,000 EIDL advance, which was a grant provided under the EIDL program that did not have to be repaid. Bank records show that Dooley allegedly spent thousands of dollars of the pandemic relief funds at a casino and none of it on business expenses. The charge of wire fraud provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000, or twice the gross gain or loss from the scheme, whichever is greater. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jeffrey Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; Justin Page, Acting Inspector in Charge of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Boston Division; and Anthony P. D’Esposito, Inspector General, Department of Labor, Office of Inspector General made the announcement. Assistant U.S. Attorney Philip C. Cheng of the Criminal Division is prosecuting the case. On March 26, 2026 , United States Attorney Leah B. Foley announced the creation of the Benefit & Voter Fraud Team, a district-wide initiative established in response to the rampant fraud being uncovered across Massachusetts. Members of the public are encouraged to report suspected benefit fraud in Massachusetts by calling 1-855-SCAM-MA-1 (855-722-6621). On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division . The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendants are presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. title: Justice Department Opens Investigation into Alleged Firearm Permitting Abuses in Two Connecticut Municipalities
body: Press Release Justice Department Opens Investigation into Alleged Firearm Permitting Abuses in Two Connecticut Municipalities Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, the Justice Department opened an investigation into Middletown and Waterbury , Connecticut, to determine whether they unnecessarily delay the issuance of firearm permits to their residents. The Second Amendment protects the right of law-abiding citizens to keep and bear firearms — including the right to carry firearms. The investigation will focus on the Middletown and Waterbury police departments’ permitting systems. “All law-abiding Americans have a constitutional right to bear arms for self‑defense,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “This right is not a luxury reserved for a privileged few, but a fundamental liberty for all, including the residents of Middletown and Waterbury, Connecticut.” The Supreme Court’s 2022 seminal ruling in New York State Rifle and Pistol Association v. Bruen , recognized that the right to keep and bear arms applies with equal force inside and outside the home. In Bruen , the Supreme Court warned against “lengthy wait times in processing license applications” that effectively “deny ordinary citizens their right to public carry.” The Middletown and Waterbury police departments may be unreasonably denying otherwise qualified applicants a CCW permit and forcing them to undergo a potentially years-long appeal process to exercise this fundamental right. The Civil Rights Division’s Second Amendment Section enforces the Second Amendment. If you believe your right to keep and bear arms is being infringed, please submit an online complaint through www.justice.gov/crt/second-amendment-section . Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Civil Rights Component Civil Rights Division Press Release Number: 26-1252

title: Arizona Man Sentenced to 38 Months in Prison for Threatening to Kill President Trump and Former Vice President Harris
body: Press Release Arizona Man Sentenced to 38 Months in Prison for Threatening to Kill President Trump and Former Vice President Harris Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Arizona PHOENIX, Ariz. – Rene Ortiz, 56, of Casa Grande, Arizona, was sentenced on Oct. 20, 2026, by Senior U.S. District Judge Stephen M. McNamee to 38 months in prison. Ortiz was convicted by a federal jury on June 8, 2026, of two felony violations of Making Threats Against Successors to the Presidency and one felony violation of Making Threats Against Former Presidents. On Nov. 5, 2024—Election Day—Ortiz delivered to the federal courthouse in Phoenix a written threat to “execute the newly elected [President of the United States] by firing an M-16A2 service rifle with a magazine of 6 rounds,” directed at both candidates, former Vice President Kamala Harris and President Donald Trump. After the election, on Nov. 25, 2024, Ortiz delivered a second threat to shoot “the incoming fraudulent elected [President of the United States] … at the inauguration on January 20th, 2025,” to the federal courthouse in Tucson. When interviewed by the U.S. Secret Service about the threats, Ortiz repeated his intent to make the threats; he was subsequently arrested on Jan. 17, 2025, ahead of the Presidential Inauguration. The United States Secret Service conducted the investigation with assistance from the United States Marshals Service. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Amy Chang and Abbie Broughton, District of Arizona, Phoenix, handled the prosecution. title: Missouri Governor and U.S. Attorneys Announce Operation Show-Me the Money to Combat Benefits Fraud
body: Press Release Missouri Governor and U.S. Attorneys Announce Operation Show-Me the Money to Combat Benefits Fraud Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Missouri JEFFERSON CITY, Mo. – R. Matthew Price, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Missouri, joined Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe, Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, and Tom Albus, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Missouri, to announce Operation Show-Me the Money , an unprecedented partnership between the State of Missouri and the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) to aggressively identify, investigate, and prosecute fraud involving taxpayer-funded benefit programs. Operation Show-Me the Money will focus on state programs that distribute federal funds to entities and individuals, bringing together state and federal resources to better identify potential fraud, strengthen oversight, and ensure taxpayer dollars are being used for their intended purpose. "Missouri is no place for fraud, and those who think they can cheat the system and steal from hardworking taxpayers are going to be held accountable," said Governor Kehoe. "From day one, my administration has made it a priority to crack down on criminals and protect taxpayer dollars. Through Operation Show-Me the Money, we're bringing the full force of state and federal law enforcement together to send a clear message: If you're stealing from Missouri taxpayers, we're coming after you." “By combining federal investigative and prosecutorial resources with the state’s knowledge and oversight of its benefit programs, we can detect fraud sooner, build stronger cases, and hold offenders accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Price. “Hardworking Missouri taxpayers deserve better, and we are committed to protecting the integrity of these programs, following the money, and using every available federal law enforcement tool to bring those who commit fraud to justice.” Operation Show-Me the Money is a collaborative effort between the Kehoe Administration, the Missouri Attorney General's Office, and the DOJ, expanding existing partnerships for cross-departmental data sharing to help identify suspicious activity and pursue prosecution. The initiative will bring together dedicated staff from the Missouri Attorney General's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit and the DOJ to strengthen coordination and investigative efforts. “Missouri will not be a safe haven for anyone who steals from taxpayers or exploits public programs," said Attorney General Hanaway. "We have won many major victories against consumer, contractor, and Medicaid fraud, but our work is not finished. We thank Governor Mike Kehoe and U.S. Attorneys, Tom and Matt, for their leadership as we work together to root out fraud and protect taxpayer dollars across our state.” “This operation will provide better access to data and information on these benefit programs and better communication between our agencies, helping us ensure that tax dollars won’t be siphoned away from these valuable programs by fraudsters,” said U.S. Attorney Albus. “I look forward to working with our state and federal partners on this valuable new initiative.” The operation will utilize a three-pronged approach, first drawing on referrals from existing state agency investigations and tips from frontline program staff. Second, investigators will conduct targeted reviews of individual benefit programs, beginning with the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), to identify suspicious activity and vulnerabilities. The third component will use data across multiple state agencies and programs to detect patterns of potential fraud that might otherwise go unnoticed. By examining information across systems, investigators can identify emerging trends and determine where further inquiry is warranted. In addition to pursuing fraud, the operation will help identify weaknesses in existing programs and opportunities to strengthen oversight. Findings may inform future administrative changes, program improvements, or legislative solutions to better safeguard taxpayer dollars and prevent fraud before it occurs. Operation Show-Me the Money builds on ongoing state and federal efforts to crack down on fraud and protect taxpayer dollars. U.S. Attorney Price recently joined Vice President JD Vance in signing the Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud , reinforcing Missouri's commitment to holding fraudsters accountable. For more information on federal efforts to combat fraud, visit justice.gov/fraud . Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Benefit Fraud Component USAO - Missouri, Western

title: Former High School Teacher Sentenced to Federal Prison for Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Former High School Teacher Sentenced to Federal Prison for Possession of Child Pornography Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas WACO, Texas – A former Belton High School teacher was sentenced to 78 months in prison for possession of child pornography, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, on Sept. 22, 2024, Pietro Victor Giustino, 40, sent Bitcoin to a vendor in exchange for child sexual abuse material. On June 4, 2025, the FBI executed a federal search warrant at Giustino’s residence in Belton and discovered devices and media containing thousands of images of child pornography, including prepubescent minors. Giustino was arrested in July 2025. He pleaded guilty in March to one count of possession of visual depictions of sexual activities by minors. On Wednesday, U.S. District Judge Christopher Wolfe sentenced Giustino to 78 months in federal prison followed by five years of supervised release. Judge Wolfe also ordered a $5,000 Victims of Trafficking Act assessment along with an Amy, Vicky, and Andy Child Pornography Assessment Act assessment of $10,000. The FBI investigated the case with assistance from the Belton Police Department and with cooperation from the Belton Independent School District. Assistant U.S. Attorney Greg Gloff prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Western

title: Little Rock Man Sentenced to 15 Years in Federal Prison for Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm
body: Press Release Little Rock Man Sentenced to 15 Years in Federal Prison for Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Arkansas Ms. Paulette Chappelle, Public Affairs Officer Paulette.Chappelle@usdoj.gov LITTLE ROCK—Andre Lavon Harris, who previously received a 30-year state sentence for first-degree murder, will spend the next 180 months in federal prison for being a felon in possession of a firearm. Jonathan D. Ross, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, which was handed down on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, by United States District Judge Lee P. Rudofsky. A federal grand jury indicted Harris, 47, of Little Rock, in a three-count Indictment for being a felon in possession of a firearm, possession with intent to distribute fentanyl, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. On July 6, 2026, Harris pleaded guilty to being a felon in possession of a firearm. Judge Rudofsky also sentenced Harris to three years’ supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. On September 5, 2023, an agent with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), working with a confidential source (CS), learned that Harris was a multi-ounce distributor of methamphetamine and fentanyl pills in Saline and Pulaski Counties. The CS advised agents that Harris wore an ankle monitor, drove a black Chevrolet Tahoe, and carried a firearm. Through their investigation, agents confirmed Harris was a convicted felon who was on parole and had a search waiver on file. On November 15, 2023, agents conducted a traffic stop on Harris to execute a parole search. During the search of Harris’ vehicle, agents located a loaded Taurus, model G3C, 9mm semi-automatic firearm on the floorboard of the driver’s side that Harris stated he got off “the street.” Agents also located in the center console’s cupholder a pill bottle containing 2.2 grams of crack cocaine, eight pills containing fentanyl, and another nine pills containing methamphetamine. Harris’ criminal history includes felony convictions for first-degree murder on July 23, 1999, possession of firearms by certain persons, and battery, second degree. This case was investigated by the DEA with assistance from the Little Rock Police Department. This case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Edward Walker of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Arkansas. # # # Additional information about the office of the United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, is available online at https://www.justice.gov/edar X (formerly known as Twitter): @USAO_EDAR Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Arkansas, Eastern

body: Press Release Worcester Man Charged with Possession with Intent to Distribute Fentanyl Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A Worcester man has been arrested and charged with possessing multiple kilograms of fentanyl intended for distribution. Junior Tejada Hernandez, 28, whose immigration status is unknown at this time, was charged with one count of possession with intent to distribute controlled substances. Hernandez was arrested yesterday and will appear in federal court in Worcester later today. According to the charging documents, during a search of Hernandez’s one-bedroom apartment yesterday, more than three kilograms of fentanyl was recovered in the bedroom. Drug paraphernalia was also located inside of a suitcase in the bedroom closet which contained cutting agents, baggies, a sifting device, a blender used to mix controlled substances and other dilutants, scissors and other materials. The charge of possession with intent to distribute fentanyl provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, at least three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $1 million. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jarod A. Forget, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration, New England Field Division; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division; Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, Boston Field Office; and Colonel Geoffrey D. Noble, Superintendent of the Massachusetts State Police made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by the Leominster, Fitchburg, Clinton, Worcester, Gardner, Lunenberg and Webster Police Departments and the Worcester County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Zachary Stendig of the Worcester Branch Office is prosecuting the case. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Boston is comprised of agents and officers from HSI, FBI, DEA, ATF, USMS, IRS-CI, USPIS, DOL-OIG, DSS and CBP as well as several state and local law enforcement agencies, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts. The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. body: Press Release Maryland Sex Offender Indicted on Failure to Register Charges Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Baltimore, Maryland – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Maryland announced, today, that a Maryland man is facing indictment for a sex-offender registration crime. Paul Revell, 42, of Pikesville, is charged with failure to register as a sex offender. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the indictment with Clinton J. Fuchs, U.S. Marshal for the District of Maryland (USMS), and Chief Robert McCullough, Baltimore County Police Department (BCPD). According to the indictment, from July 16, 2026, through August 14, 2026, Revell, who is a convicted sex offender, knowingly failed to update a registration as is required by the Sex Offender Registration Notification Act under Federal law. If convicted, Revell faces a maximum of 10 years in federal prison for failure to register as a sex offender. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. This case is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse.  Led by the United States Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims.  For more information about Project Safe Childhood, visit justice.gov/psc .  For more information about Internet safety education, visit justice.gov/psc and click on the “Resources” tab on the left of the page. U.S. Attorney Hayes commended USMS and BCPD for their work in the investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Maryam Zhuravitsky who is prosecuting the federal case. title: Massachusetts Man Convicted of Transporting a Minor with Intent to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity
body: Press Release Massachusetts Man Convicted of Transporting a Minor with Intent to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A Pittsfield, Mass. man has been convicted by a federal jury in Springfield of transporting a minor with intent to engage in sexual activity. Paul Newton-Irelan, 53, was found guilty of transporting a minor with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. U.S. District Court Judge Mark G. Mastroianni scheduled sentencing for Feb. 1, 2026. Newton-Irelan was indicted by a federal grand jury in April 2024 . On Nov. 26, 2023, Newton-Irelan transported a minor victim, an 11-year-old child, from New York to Massachusetts, with the intent that the minor would engage in sexual activity for which any person can be charged with a criminal offense, namely, rape and abuse of a child. The charge of transportation of a minor with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity provides for a sentence of at least 10 years and up to life in prison, no less than five years of supervised release and up to supervised release for life and a $250,000 fine. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England made the announcement. Substantial assistance was provided by the Pittsfield Police Department and the Schenectady Police Department. Valuable assistance was provided by the Schenectady County District Attorney’s Office and the Berkshire County District Attorney’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Caroline Merck and David Tobin of the Criminal Division prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Child predator sentenced to more than 27 years in federal prison for sexual exploitation of a minor
body: Press Release Child predator sentenced to more than 27 years in federal prison for sexual exploitation of a minor Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas FORT WORTH, Texas — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced a Fort Worth man, who has a previous conviction for sexual offenses against a child, was sentenced to 327 months in federal prison for sexually exploiting a minor on Sept. 29. Travis Jerrad McQuiston Reed, 34, pleaded guilty in April to one count of sexual exploitation of a child. “The federal government has no tolerance for anyone who preys on children, and today’s sentence reflects that reality,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Anyone who believes they can exploit a child in North Texas and escape accountability is gravely mistaken. In this District, federal law enforcement will find you, we will prosecute you and you will face a sentence measured in decades as the defendant is in this case. I am grateful to our partners at CBP and HSI for their swift work that stopped Reed from continuing to harm children.” “The steadfast vigilance of our CBP officers at the Port of Galveston directly interrupted a dangerous threat and set a comprehensive federal investigation into motion,” said Acting Director of Field Operations Leslie Fleming-Luczkowski. “Thanks to the seamless collaboration between our frontline personnel, Homeland Security Investigations, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office, a predator has been brought to justice with a significant federal sentence. We remain unwavering in our commitment to protecting the most vulnerable and dismantling child exploitation networks” According to court documents, on or about Sept. 7, 2025, Reed enticed a minor victim to engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing visual depictions. U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers encountered Reed as he re-entered the United States at the Port of Galveston, Texas, on Nov. 2, 2025. During a lawful inspection of his iPhone, officers discovered nude images of children and referred the device for forensic analysis. The subsequent review confirmed that Reed produced the child sexual abuse material in Fort Worth using the same device. Court documents also show that Reed had a prior felony conviction for indecency with a child in Tarrant County, which subjected him to enhanced penalties. Reed has also agreed to pay restitution, mandatory assessments and will be required to register as a sex offender upon release. U.S. Customs and Border Protection and Homeland Security Investigations Dallas conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Aisha Saleem from the Fort Worth Division prosecuted the case. Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Texas, Northern

title: U.S. Attorney’s Office for Northern Ohio Joins DOJ Fraud Division and USDA in Uncovering Nearly $42M in SNAP Benefit Fraud
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office for Northern Ohio Joins DOJ Fraud Division and USDA in Uncovering Nearly $42M in SNAP Benefit Fraud Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio 13 U.S. Attorney’s Offices joined the Fraud Division in bringing enforcement actions against alleged fraudsters CLEVELAND – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio announced several enforcement actions as part of a nationwide effort led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) targeting suspected fraudulent activity in the Supplemental Nutritional Assistance Program (SNAP). SNAP is a federal benefits program funded by the USDA and administered by the State of Ohio. The Northern District of Ohio (NDOH) was a key participant in this surge effort. Between Sept. 1 and Oct. 21, 2026, the Fraud Division and 13 U.S. Attorney’s Offices across the country participated in the Department’s first National USDA Benefits and Program Fraud Enforcement Surge. This coordinated effort resulted in actions against more than 40 defendants whose alleged or proven schemes caused nearly $45 million in intended losses to the federal government. Nearly $42 million of that amount involved fraud against SNAP benefits, which provide monthly food assistance to low-income individuals and families. “You cannot exchange food program benefits for cash, illegal drugs, or anything else - it is a violation of federal law,” said U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer for the Northern District of Ohio. “My office will aggressively protect the integrity of taxpayer-funded programs to assist those truly in need. During some of these investigations, we also found evidence of federal housing or drug trafficking violations. Together with our investigative partners, we will find and prosecute those who attempt to manipulate federal programs for their own benefit.” “These benefits are a critical lifeline for eligible families, not a source of profit for those willing to exploit the program,” said Lewis Porcella, Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Secret Service Cleveland Field Office. “Secret Service investigators will work relentlessly with our law enforcement partners to uncover fraud and hold accountable anyone who steals resources intended to help vulnerable Americans put food on the table.” NDOH Notable Cases • United States v. Sqar Qahtan, Mohsin Mohsin, Baligh Naji, Mariah Hatcher, Ahmed Al Hamami, and Almotawakil Nassr (Complaints) – approximately $1,000,000 in intended loss On Oct. 6, 2026, Sqar Qahtan, 31, Baligh Naji, 34, Ahmed Al Hamami, 36, all citizens of Yemen residing in Euclid, Ohio, along with Mohsin Mohsin, 28, of Syracuse, New York; Mariah Hatcher, 30, of Euclid, Ohio, and Almotawakil Nassr, 29, of Detroit, Michigan, were charged in criminal complaints with SNAP Benefits Fraud, Wire Fraud, and Conspiracy to Commit Wire Fraud. SNAP benefits are more commonly known as “food stamps.” For approximately two years, the defendants allegedly operated a conspiracy to exchange Ohio SNAP benefit cards for cash, marijuana, and other non-SNAP items while employed at a gas station convenience store in Euclid, Ohio. Identified members of the conspiracy obtained at least $64,000 in SNAP benefits, with the members of the conspiracy likely to have engaged in at least approximately $1 million in fraud. If convicted, each defendant faces per count: SNAP Benefits Fraud – five years in prison; Wire Fraud – 20 years in prison; and Conspiracy to Commit Wire Fraud – 20 years in prison. The investigation was conducted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture-Office of the Inspector General, U.S. Secret Service-Money Laundering Task Force, Ohio Investigative Unit, FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, and the Euclid Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Erica Barnhill leads the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. • United States v. Glenda K. Jordan (Indictment) – approximately $162,580 in intended loss On Sept. 9, 2026, Glenda K. Jordan, 63, of Painesville, Ohio, was charged with three counts of Bank Fraud, Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud, Theft of Government Property, and Supplemental Security Income Fraud-Knowing Concealment. For more than a decade, Jordan allegedly engaged in a scheme to mislead government agencies to fraudulently obtain SNAP benefits, HUD-funded housing benefits, and Supplemental Security Income benefits. On numerous official government documents, she lied about—and concealed—her marriage, her husband's income, and her true residence. In one instance, Jordan concealed her scheme by reporting her sister-in-law as her ‘live-in aide’ when in fact, her sister-in-law used Jordan’s subsidized unit as her primary home. Meanwhile, Jordan resided at a different location with her husband. If convicted, she faces prison sentences of up to 30 years per Bank Fraud count; 30 years for Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud; 10 years for Theft of Government Property; and five years for Supplemental Security Income Fraud-Knowing Concealment. The investigation was conducted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture-Office of the Inspector General, Social Security Administration-Office of the Inspector General, and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development-Office of the Inspector General. Special Assistant United States Attorney Jason White is leading the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. • United States v. Myron Cage and Raymond Stevens (Complaints) – approximately $4,070 in intended loss On Sept. 30, 2026, Myron Cage, 43, of Garfield Heights, and Dwayne Stevens, 34, of Mayfield Heights, were charged with SNAP Benefits Fraud as part of a related drug trafficking operation. Between February and August 2022, Cage and Stevens allegedly obtained SNAP benefits that they received as payment, or partial payment, for crack cocaine at a corner store in Cleveland that Cage owned and operated. During search warrants executed at their residences, agents also seized more than 500 grams of packaged cocaine. If convicted, they each face up to five years in prison for SNAP Benefits Fraud offenses, and up to 40 years in prison on related drug charges. The investigation was conducted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture-Office of the Inspector General, the DEA, and the FBI Assistant United States Attorneys Robert F. Corts , Marc D. Bullard , and Samuel V. Lioi are leading the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. For a list of similar enforcement actions across the country, please visit justice.gov/opa/pr/dojs-fraud-division-department-agriculture-and-usda-oig-uncover-nearly-42m-snap-benefit . On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division . The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud—a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance—to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. A complaint, or indictment, are merely allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Contact Jessica Salas Novak Jessica.Salas.Novak@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Fraud Components National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - Ohio, Northern

SNAP is a federal benefits program funded by the USDA and administered by the State of Ohio. The Northern District of Ohio was a key participant in this surge effort.

title: Arizona man sentenced to 3 years in prison for smuggling meth into Montana
body: Press Release Arizona man sentenced to 3 years in prison for smuggling meth into Montana Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana BILLINGS – A Phoenix man who smuggled meth from Arizona to Billings was sentenced today to three years and one month in prison, followed by four years of supervised release, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Steger Smith said. Sebastian Kessamer Gilder, Jr., 28, pleaded guilty in June 2025 to possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine. U.S. District Judge Kathleen S. Lane presided. The government alleged in court documents that Gilder came to the attention of law enforcement in 2021 when the Eastern Montana High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area Taskforce was in the midst of investigating a Sonora, Mexico-based drug smuggling ring known locally as “The Village.” The Village smuggled drugs from Mexico into Phoenix and then used couriers to move them into Montana by bus, personal vehicles, and the U.S. Postal Service. The shipments usually were coordinated by individuals in Hermosillo and Nogales, Sonora, Mexico. Gilder, who lived in Phoenix, was recruited by the Village to transport illicit drugs to Billings. Investigators were aware of his movements and arranged a drug buy using an undercover agent on Jan. 13, 2021. The agent successfully bought a pound of methamphetamine off Gilder, which eventually led to his arrest. This operation is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Montana comprises agents and officers from various law enforcement agencies with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Montana. The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted this case. The Eastern Montana High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area Taskforce conducted the investigation. Contact Keri Leggett Acting Public Affairs Officer keri.leggett@usdoj.gov Updated October 22, 2026 Topic Homeland Security Task Force Component USAO - Montana Press Release Number: 26-273

title: Former Suffolk County Corrections Officer Sentenced for COVID Unemployment and Loan Fraud
body: Press Release Former Suffolk County Corrections Officer Sentenced for COVID Unemployment and Loan Fraud Thursday, October 22, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A former Suffolk County Corrections Officer was sentenced yesterday in federal court in Boston for COVID unemployment and loan fraud. Jasmine Murphy, 39, of Cambridge, Mass. was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Richard G. Stearns to time served (one day in prison) and two years of supervised release. The defendant was also ordered to pay $19,868 in restitution to the Department of Unemployment Assistance and $17,708 restitution to the Small Business Administration. In April 2026 , Murphy pleaded guilty to seven counts of wire fraud and one count of false statements to a financial institution. Murphy was charged in December 2024 . Murphy had been a corrections officer with the Suffolk County Sherriff’s Department from January 2022 to December 2024. Murphy fraudulently applied for pandemic unemployment and small business loan benefits while working for a workforce services company. While employed by that company, Murphy collected approximately $37,576 in unemployment benefits and small business loan funds. In Murphy’s PUA application, Murphy made fraudulent representations about her employment status and thereafter falsely claimed, on a weekly basis, that she did not work and did not receive any income during the prior week. In Murphy’s PPP loan application, Murphy submitted false statements to SBA-approved lenders, including the income and/or payroll of her purported small businesses, in order to obtain her loan. Murphy also made false representations on forms submitted to request that her PPP loan be forgiven. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Kelly M.  Lawson, Special Agent in Charge, U.S. Department of Labor, Office of Inspector General; and Inspector General Joseph V. Cuffari, Ph.D., U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Office of Inspector General, made the announcement. Assistant U.S. Attorney Dustin Chao, Chief of the Public Corruption & Special Prosecutions Unit, prosecuted the case. Updated October 22, 2026 Topics COVID-Related Fraud Financial Fraud Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: We are working with Voltus to build a 1-gigawatt virtual power plant.
body: We are working with Voltus to build a 1-gigawatt virtual power plant. Oct 22, 2026 Today, Google and Voltus announced an expanded agreement to build a 1-gigawatt (GW) virtual power plant across the PJM grid region, which serves 67 million people across 13 states and Washington, D.C. Voltus aggregates flexible capacity from local businesses and homes — like smart thermostats, batteries, and industrial assets — into a Google-funded virtual power plant. During peak demand, these assets temporarily reduce energy use to support grid reliability. In return, participating customers receive direct economic benefits, including bill savings and cash payments. Building on a 100-megawatt agreement from earlier this year, this 10-fold expansion represents one of the largest known distributed capacity portfolios deployed by a hyperscaler to date. This initiative reflects Google’s commitment to actively bring new capacity to local grids while strengthening regional reliability and affordability.

title: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence
body: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence From transaction foundation models to sovereign cloud deployments, leading financial institutions across Europe are scaling intelligent technologies with advanced computing. October 21, 2026 by Jason Renders 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure. Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA , powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs , Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x. “Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.” Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Training on Accelerated Infrastructure Starling Bank , the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data. Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases. SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls. Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them. Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer. NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR. Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model. Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads. Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the Polars GPU engine , accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. RavenPack built a dataset generation pipeline on Bigdata.com that takes a plain-language research hypothesis and returns a labeled, backtest-ready dataset — running on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron model. Investors can use these datasets to identify, analyze and visualize market trends. Speeding Data Pipelines to Improve Fraud Detection RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and NVIDIA cuDF help accelerate data processing across multi-terabyte-scale, siloed, regulated sources, compressing the time from data to decision for fraud and other scenarios. HSBC provides near-real-time client insights that support customer processes and on-demand decision-making while minimizing risk and fraud, powered by 5x faster data processing on Starburst Enterprise’s GPU Engine . Stripe , a global provider of programmable financial services, sees 42x faster data pipelines and 92% cost savings for its Stripe Radar fraud-detection platform with NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Ray Data in offline testing. This enables Stripe Radar’s machine learning pipelines to continuously optimize model training and improve fraud detection. Learn more about NVIDIA accelerated computing in financial services . title: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models
body: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models New tools joining NVIDIA Cosmos are helping accelerate data pipelines, train, evaluate and optimize world models more efficiently, and improve accuracy at lower cost. October 21, 2026 by Pranjali Joshi 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To help developers rapidly build world models , which help physical AI systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open models — as well as data, training and optimization tools and recipes — to scale training data, adapt models, test behavior and optimize for performance before deployment. Build Better Training Data Building world models begins with multimodal, multisensory data. NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory brings together the tools and skills for labeling, curating, augmenting and evaluating data at scale for training physical AI. Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets, has now added support for multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Cosmos Data Factory now offers the following five cloud-native blueprints and is available through GitHub , Microsoft Azure , Nebius and CoreWeave : Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation: Curates and labels driving data, then adds synthetic examples of hard-to-capture scenarios to expand training coverage. Image Attribute Augmentation: Varies object appearance to improve image search. Event Video Generation: Turns still images into synthetic videos of rare or unsafe events. Defect Image Generation: Generates printed circuit board, metal and glass defect images for inspection models. Video Data Augmentation: Changes weather and lighting in existing footage while preserving scene structure. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/CDF-visual-Oct20.mp4 Cosmos Data Factory accelerates data curation, processing and synthetic data generation with agentic skills. Companies are already putting Cosmos Data Factory blueprints to work to speed their physical AI development workflows. Porsche is leading the development of a shared AV data flywheel across Volkswagen Group brands, using Cosmos Data Factory through Voxel51 on Microsoft Azure. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Porche-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 Porsche searching and augmenting autonomous vehicle data footage in Voxel51, powered by Cosmos Data Factory. ANYbotics generated over 1,500 synthetic video clips with Cosmos Data Factory blueprints, curating real-world data and validating outputs with Encord’s platform, to train its industrial-inspection robots to recognize liquid spills and other changes between facility visits. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ANYbotics-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 ANYbotic s generating anomaly clips with Encord powered by NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory. Ultralytics , a computer vision company, retrained its YOLO model with real images and targeted synthetic defects generated using Cosmos Data Factory, improving defect localization and recall. Train, Adapt and Optimize Models With training data prepared, developers may train their own architecture or start with a pretrained model. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA extended Cosmos Framework training, optimization and deployment tools and recipes as agent skills to more open models, along with Cosmos 3, giving world model builders a faster path from experimentation to deployment. Developers and agents can now adapt open models like GR00T , Alpamayo , QWEN, Pi0.5 and other compatible Hugging Face models through fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, optimize the model with distillation and quantization, and deploy with high-performing inference. Cosmos Framework is an open, modular framework of model training and optimization tools and skills to accelerate world model development. To develop a world model specialized for egocentric manipulation, robotics research lab MicroAGI post-trained Cosmos 3 on videos of humans manipulating objects and distilled its 32-billion-parameter reasoner down to an 8-billion-parameter Nano model with no loss in accuracy. Developers can label data and post-train Cosmos 3 on Roboflow for their specific environments and tasks, then deploy those models to RoboFlow hosted or on-premises NVIDIA GPUs to bring video reasoning into factories and warehouses. Test Policies and Run Models Faster Alongside these tools, NVIDIA continues advancing foundational technology through its work on Cosmos models. New Cosmos 3 Nano model variants for simulation enable developers to test autonomous policies in repeatable, hard-to-capture, multiview multisensor scenarios. Accompanying code allows developers to adapt the models to train and evaluate their own policies for autonomous vehicles and bimanual robots in interactive simulations before real-world testing. Multiview and multisensory video data generation for evaluating policies in closed loop simulation. Developers can deploy core Cosmos models using updated NVIDIA Cosmos 3 NIM microservices, which deliver up to 2x faster inference with no quality loss in validated configurations, while continuous video analysis enables sub-second alerts. For vision AI developers, the new NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) 3.3 , built on Cosmos NIM microservices, turns one prompt into an efficient video AI application and helps teams monitor 40% more video streams with the same GPU. ADNOC uses Fogsphere’s MistIQ agentic platform , built with Cosmos and the NVIDIA Metropolis VSS Blueprint , to detect safety hazards in real time across 65 sites. For rare events, Fogsphere also uses the Cosmos Data Factory to generate synthetic training data, improving detection without needing to physically stage dangerous situations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ADNOC-Cosmos.mp4 The Cosmos platform is fully modular and open. Developers can use Cosmos Data Factory to generate training datasets, Cosmos Framework to train and adapt world models, then deploy supported Cosmos models through NIM microservices . title: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck
body: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck Companies around the world are using the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run AI factories as one system and unlock infrastructure development. October 21, 2026 by Vladimir Troy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem. Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues. One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together: NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground. NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets. NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations. GE Vernova is deploying its grid-to-facility and rack power expertise to complement NVIDIA DSX systems, enabling customers to transform power constraints into competitive advantages while maximizing compute and token output, sustainability and grid reliability. Hitachi Energy ’s battery energy storage system has qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready ,  helping customers identify power infrastructure that meets applicable NVIDIA DSX reference architecture design requirements for resilient, reliable and scalable AI factories. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA and ETAP, is advancing NVIDIA DSX with validated NVIDIA Vera Rubin power and cooling reference architectures and an NVIDIA Omniverse -powered AI factory digital twin. Combining AVEVA ’s engineering software expertise with NVIDIA SimReady assets, OpenUSD and Omniverse enables connecting simulations, real-time operational data and AI-driven optimization across AVEVA, Schneider Electric and third-party solutions. Together, these capabilities help organizations design, simulate, operate and optimize data centers across their lifecycle, improving energy efficiency and workload performance while accelerating time to token. Siemens Energy is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA by developing a reference design for resilient, scalable and grid-aware power infrastructure across power generation, transmission and distribution. This design is aligned with the requirements of the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factory design. The company is also exploring usingNVIDIA technologies such as RAPIDS, Metropolis and Isaac Sim for its Noedra digital twin platform, evaluating how the technologies could enhance grid infrastructure monitoring, identify emerging risks and support unplanned outage prevention. Phaidra integrated DSX Flex, DSX Max-Q and DSX Exchange into its self-learning agents, optimizing cooling and power allocation to maximize tokens per watt, improve grid flexibility and deliver about 10% more compute within the same power envelope. Emerald AI integrated its Conductor platform into DSX Flex to help utilities tap underused grid capacity, an approach modeled to unlock up to 100 gigawatts on the existing U.S. grid. Explore the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint and the Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory Reference Design . Learn more from NVIDIA and energy leaders who are accelerating power-flexible AI factories to strengthen the grid at GTC Berlin. Visit Hitachi Energy (booth 7004, hall 7), Schneider Electric (booth 3041, hall 3) and Siemens Energy (booth 3048, hall 3) and tune into sessions with Schneider Electric on Wednesday, Oct. 21: From Grid to AI: Engineering the Future of AI Factories and Energy Intelligence: Powering the AI Era . title: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations
body: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations October 21, 2026 by Mavi Nafria 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. A production ready prototype deployed inside Zooplus ’ Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment achieved 86% search accuracy using the NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever library for semantic search and the NVIDIA Blueprint for retail catalog enrichment for generated, search-ready product attributes. Photoroom results from its deployment with Vestiaire Collective , where its Image Editing API now standardizes every primary image,  about 40,000 a day across 70 countries, at the point of listing. Listings processed by Photoroom sold at a 5% higher rate of liquidity, with 3% to 7% more unique views per product page . The pipeline runs on NVIDIA GPUs with TensorRT and Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot can help users quickly respond to demand spikes. Omi launched ProductDrop, a workflow that anchors every generated image to an approved digital twin, letting brands scale creative output across entire catalogs without introducing product errors . L’Oréal is using this approach, combining Omi ’s digital twins with generated brand environments within its CreAItech program. Omi runs TRELLIS 3D asset generation on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, speeding up inference by 10x and reducing pipeline latency by 4x. In addition, L’Oréal is accelerating the discovery of the best ingredient combinations, moving from months of experimentation to hours of computational screening, with the integration of NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflow. L’Oréal is also testing this approach with CurieOS, Orbital Industries ‘ operating system for science and engineering, using OrbMol-v2, its open source molecular simulation model. Integrated with the NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit and powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, OrbMol-v2 is five times faster than comparable models and delivers 21% lower error than the next-best model of its kind. This AI-based workflow enables researchers to identify the most promising ingredient combinations for solubilizing UV filters and optimizing performance before committing to laboratory testing. Mirakl , a software company for intelligent commerce, runs open models on NVIDIA GPUs, both on its own infrastructure and through European cloud providers like Scaleway . This keeps its technology sovereign, avoids vendor lock-in and delivers the speed and scale its customers expect . Mirakl ’s Catalog Transformer pairs fine-tuned open models with proprietary services and has onboarded more than 70 million products, turning messy vendor data into accurate, well-organized catalogs. Physical Intelligence Enables Training in Simulation NVIDIA physical AI, digital twins and open models help simulate retail environments, automate warehouse operations and deliver virtual try-on experiences for European retailers and fashion brands. Otto Group advanced its autonomous warehouse under human supervision initiative — built with Reply on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and running on Google Cloud — to the group’s largest fulfillment center in Haldensleben, Germany. New capabilities let logistics teams design, test and optimize warehouse operations entirely in simulation before any physical implementation . ALLSIDES launched its 3D Digital Twin Factory: an automated pipeline that transforms physical objects into SimReady 3D digital twins in minutes, capturing sub-millimeter geometric accuracy, measured physical properties and fully relightable materials that maintain accuracy under any lighting condition. Those digital twins serve as the foundation for simulating entire store layouts in 3D, as well as for tracking products reliably throughout the shopping journey and at checkout regardless of ambient light. Built on NVIDIA CUDA, OptiX and TensorRT, the platform already serves brands including adidas , Amazon , Nike , Zalando and Zara . CATCHES achieved production results from its RealFit deployment with AMIRI of conversion up 55%, add-to-cart up 80% and gross sales up 56% , all after seasonal adjustment against like-for-like styles. The company launched PredictiveFit, extending physics-based virtual try-on to retailers, as well as CASI, a personal fashion agent that shops, styles and sizes for customers over WhatsApp, powered by open weight models including NVIDIA Nemotron 3, built on NVIDIA Omniverse and the Newton Physics Engine. Explore New NVIDIA Retail Blueprints at the Nebius Booth At GTC Berlin, Nebius is showcasing three NVIDIA Blueprints for retail , all available in early access and running on Nebius infrastructure, accelerated by NVIDIA: Agent Harness for Employee Productivity : An agentic assistant that consolidates scheduling, task management, inventory alerts and operational insights for store managers. Inventory Simulation and Optimization: A blueprint that can help retailers reduce overstock and stockouts by modeling demand scenarios, testing replenishment strategies and optimizing stock levels before users need to commit in the real world. Agentic Finetuning Flywheel: A self-improving loop that uses agentic workflows to continuously generate training data, fine-tune open source models and feed real-world performance back into the next training cycle. Request early access to the blueprints and learn more about NVIDIA technologies for retail and consumer packaged goods . See notice regarding software product information.
